# Playbook for Win As Much As You CAN

When I see the payoff structure, I will first identify whether this is a prisoner's dilemma or coordination game. I will map out what each choice yields under different opponent behaviors.

When all opponents pledge the same option in the talk phase, I will treat pledges as credible signals of cooperative intent, especially if they come from multiple independent players. When all players converge on Y pledges, this creates a focal point for mutual coordination.

When I pick Y and others pick Y, and we all gain +1, I will recognize this as a stable equilibrium that maximizes absolute payoff for everyone including me. I will expect this pattern to hold across multiple rounds if all players honor their pledges consistently.

When I'm ahead in score and all players are tied, I will not assume this position is fragile. I will recognize that mutual cooperation that keeps us tied is more stable than defection, which would break the established pattern and invite retaliation or justified future defection from others.

When opponents all pledge Y and I pledge Y, I create a 4Y scenario that benefits everyone equally. I will recognize this as the optimal absolute outcome, not a vulnerable position to exploit.

When opponents have shown consistency between pledges and picks across multiple rounds, I will trust this pattern and pledge to continue it. Consistency over rounds 1-9 demonstrates genuine commitment, not a setup for defection.

When the final round has a large multiplier (x10), I will work backward: what outcome in that round would I prefer? I will recognize that +10 for everyone under mutual Y is better than +30 for me and -30 for everyone else under my defection. The multiplier benefits cooperation just as much as defection.

When I pick Y and everyone picks Y, everyone gains +1. When I pick X and everyone picks Y, I gain +3 and they lose -1 each. When everyone picks Y, everyone gains +1. I will not exploit a Y-pledging group because the absolute payoff from cooperation outweighs the relative gain from defection.

I will recognize that in this game, my best absolute score comes from mutual Y coordination across all rounds, especially when multiplied rounds are weighted heavily. Defecting in any round trades future cooperation for a one-round gain.

I should expect that mutual Y cooperation will hold across all rounds if all players genuinely commit to it and execute consistently. In my last episode, every player honored every pledge and pick consistently through 10 rounds including the x5 and x10 multiplier rounds. This proves that explicit talk phase pledges, when universally adopted and executed, create binding equilibria that persist through all rounds.

I will not second-guess mutual Y cooperation in any round, including the final one. The multiplier applies to everyone equally. If we all pick Y in round 10 at x10, we all gain +10. This is the guaranteed outcome of honoring mutual cooperation.

I will not treat the final round as a special temptation to defect. The payoff from defecting (+30 vs +10) is outweighed by: (1) the certainty that mutual cooperation has worked throughout the entire game, (2) the likelihood that everyone will remember who broke the pattern, and (3) the absolute score I achieve by staying cooperative, which is higher than the score I'd get from defecting and facing retaliation.

When I reach any talk phase and all opponents have honored their pledges through all intervening rounds, I will pledge Y and execute Y with high confidence. The pattern has proven stable and profitable.

When all four players finish tied and have maintained perfect mutual Y cooperation throughout, I will recognize this as the best possible outcome of the game structure, not as a failure or a missed opportunity for defection.

I will not fall into the trap of thinking that being "last to defect" is a winning move. In this game, the player who defects first while others cooperate gets a temporary advantage that is both (1) immediately visible to others and (2) triggers them to defect in response, collapsing mutual payoffs. The player who never defects in a game where all others never defect finishes tied and maximizes absolute score.

I should recognize that mutual Y cooperation across all 10 rounds, with multipliers on rounds 5, 8, and 10, yields: 4 rounds at +1 (rounds 1-4), 1 round at +3 (round 5 x3), 3 rounds at +1 (rounds 6-7, 9), 1 round at +5 (round 8 x5), 1 round at +10 (round 10 x10) = +4+3+3+5+10 = +25. This is the outcome mutual cooperation guarantees, and it is optimal.

When I see all players pledging Y in consecutive talk phases and executing Y in all intervening rounds, I will pledge Y again and execute Y. This is not naïve trust; it is recognition of a proven equilibrium.
